name: AED (automated external defibrillator)

comps.spec: Non-rechargeable lithium battery pack, about 9–15V, date-stamped; some models take loose CR123A-size cells
comps.loc: Slide-in pack on the back or side

comps.spec: Energy-storage capacitor, roughly 100–200 µF charged to about 1.5–2 kV — can hold a lethal charge; leave it to someone trained to discharge it
comps.loc: Inside the case, the largest part

comps.spec: Small flyback transformer that charges the capacitor
High-voltage relays or IGBTs that route the shock

notes: A working AED saves lives: leave it in its cabinet and check the battery and pad dates. Strip only broken or long-expired units. The spare battery pack is the easy prize.
